cells.tense: Here is where you are now, and what you notice keeps deepening instead of closing.
cells.act: say what you see in them only if they ask
cells.ask: When you catch a shape in someone close to you, sit on it. Speak only if they ask, and then hand it over without steering what they do with it.
cells.core:
You catch the shape a moment is making while you are still inside the moment, and catching it usually makes the thing clearer rather than settling it. It stays open. Whole situations — an argument, a family mood, a job gone stale — show their pattern without your leaving the room they happen in, and the pattern is not a verdict. It still has somewhere to go.

What this stretch invites is feeling-with rather than another read. Sit with someone inside what they are carrying, ask nothing of them, and keep your own two feet under you while you do. Not merged, not held off. That closeness does not dull what you catch. It sets it down where it can be used.
cells.sheetLine: What you catch keeps deepening because you are still in it.
cells.verb: Seeing the shape a moment makes and staying inside it while the seeing happens.
cells.place: Where pattern shows up stripped of what it is made of, and the shape alone is what can be seen.

cells.tense: You are holding a shape that has not happened yet, and the grip is already tight.
cells.act: refuse the second thing so the first can have you
cells.ask: Two reads of one situation are pulling at you. Let the second wait. Keep the one under your hand, and give it your whole attention.
cells.core:
Reading a thing fast has bent into reading it hard. You see the pattern beneath the pattern, and at some point plain noticing becomes a ruling — the verdict arrives before the moment has had its chance to surprise you. That is the same clear sight, running past what is actually here. Seeing is not the trouble. Seeing past the moment is.

Direction brings it back to size. One thing observed at a time, chosen on purpose. Not the whole drain of everything happening — simply one thing, held long enough to be understood. That is the shape clear sight takes when it does well, and it still sees far. It stops seeing so far past the table that the person across it has no room left.

cells.tense: The pattern is what you keep reaching for, and you remain at the edge of it, watching.
cells.act: open the thing you have been assuming you knew and look at it unlabelled
cells.ask: Take a thing you are sure you know cold. Open it with no name on it and look before you sort it. Nobody else needs to be there.
cells.core:
The shape of things is what you keep going after, and the going after has become a pause. You check how everything works underneath what it shows, and then you set your finding down before it is ever used. Seeing true things across situations is happening. Nothing you stand on comes out of it. Each pattern gets made and set aside again.

Reach for what has not been decided rather than one more read. Leave a thing open and meet it before you know what it is. Freshness does not need effort forced into it, only a door no one has marked. Take that one, and what you catch has somewhere to land.

cells.tense: You are writing from here right now, and the pen rests while you study what you already made.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: A giving you make quietly, a receiving you wave off. Let both pass through this time — out and in — and hold no tally of either.
cells.core:
The pattern-sight is working through you and your account of it has gone quiet. You name the shape in other people's situations, or you demote your own read to a guess after it has already proven right. What you catch goes unnamed while it does its work. You can see how a thing differs from what it claims to be, and your story has that only happening around other people.

Equity: an exchange that moves both directions. Take in what is owed you, and let what you notice be known as yours. Nothing changes in what you can see. It changes who gets credited with seeing it.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person has refused anything, so for Too Little I describe where they stand — looking for the shape of it without landing on it — and say nothing about what they turned down or why. A reader could reasonably say the opposite, that they landed somewhere long ago and are still standing there; the ask works either way, because opening one thing you assume you already know tests a landing as much as it tests a search. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you can see how everything works' — it flatters the read instead of showing the bend, so I have replaced it with the plain seam between noticing and an opinion.
